so there is no all-or-nothing rollback — atomicity and partial success are
mutually exclusive; wrap the call in a transaction if you want the former.
*Lives in:* `packages/junction/src/core/envelope.ts` (`BulkFailure`,
`toBulkFailure`, `partitionBulk`, `BULK_FAILURES`), `src/core/litestone.ts`.

### <a id="fjs-d79"></a>2026-08-02 · `FJS-D79` — One event origin, and broadcasting is declared on the service.
A mutation is announced ONCE, in `callService`, and fans out to two consumers:
the in-process bus (`posts:created`) and the channel manager (`posts created`).
They were independent origins, which cost three separate things: two places
derived the event name and disagreed; `ctx.dispatch = false` suppressed the
socket but not the bus, so a hook that deliberately withheld a broadcast still
handed the record to every server-side subscriber including webhook fan-out;
and an app that forgot to wire the publish hook had half a real-time layer with
no signal. `ctx.dispatch` is now the single switch for both — `false` announces
nothing, any other value replaces the payload.

**The separator is the discriminator, and it is not decoration.** A colon means
the in-process bus, a space means the wire — `posts:created` is a server-side
reaction (webhooks register exactly these), `posts created` is a frame a browser
receives. Two audiences with different semantics: the bus is synchronous and
unfiltered, the socket obeys channel membership and can be suppressed. Keeping
one spelling for both would make a log line and a subscription unreadable as to
which layer they belong to, and would make a subscriber wired to the wrong one
look correct — which is precisely how jetty came to subscribe on the WIRE to
`${name}:created`, the bus spelling (`FJS-059`). Colon is also the conventional
NESTING character and junction already nests with it (`webhook:delivered`),
while the browser client's parse is exact-two (`split(' ')`, `parts.length === 2`
in `client/index.ts`) — so the two separators are doing different jobs rather
than the same job twice. Do not unify them, and do not swap them: the swap
lands Feathers muscle memory on the side where it is most misleading, since
junction's payload semantics are not Feathers'.

A service declares its target with **`channel:`** — `'posts'`, a
`(rows, ctx) => Channel` function, or `false` for a declared opt-out. Named
`channel` and NOT `publish` because "publish" is an ordinary action name
(publishing a draft — the openapi suite has exactly that service) and reserving
it as an option key would stop a service from having one. A noun cannot collide
with a verb-shaped action.
**Bulk writes announce once per record**, as Feathers does: the browser's
created/patched/removed handlers each take one record, so a single event
carrying an array lands as one malformed upsert.
*Lives in:* `packages/junction/src/core/service.ts` — `callService`,
`announceToChannels`, `ChannelDeclaration`.

### <a id="fjs-d80"></a>2026-08-02 · `FJS-D80` — Broadcasting is opt-in in the framework, opt-out in the scaffold.
`createService({ name, model })` broadcasts nothing. `@@allow` row policies are
enforced when a row is READ, and a broadcast does not re-evaluate them per
subscriber — so a default of "announce everything" hands every connection in a
channel rows it could never have fetched. This is exactly Feathers' split: its
core publishes nothing without a publisher, and its *generator* scaffolds
`app.publish(() => app.channel('authenticated'))` — the line its own docs then
tell you to replace. `fli make:model` / `make:scaffold` emit `channel: '<name>'`
with the scoping warning attached, so a generated app is live out of the box and
the line is in front of the developer who has to narrow it.
*Since (2026-08-18, `FJS-334`):* an app may register ONE fallback,
`app.channels.announceDefault(fn)`, consulted only where a service declares
nothing — so the opt-in above is unchanged (there is no default until an app
writes one) while an app with one scoping rule for twenty services writes it
once. It is a default and not a second broadcaster: `channel:` is never asked
it, `channel: false` refuses it, and nothing can send one record twice. **No
string form** — a single channel name for every service is exactly the shape
this ruling refuses, so the fallback is handed the record and decides per
record. Because that inverts the failure mode — a forgotten `channel:` used to
mean a screen that never updates, and now means a broadcast on somebody else's
rule — the plugin names at boot which services fall through, and `channel: false`
takes them off the list.

*Lives in:* `packages/cli/commands/make/model.md`, `packages/cli/commands/make/scaffold.md`;
rationale in `announceToChannels()`, the fallback in
`packages/junction/src/transport/channels.ts` (`announceDefault`).

### <a id="fjs-d74"></a>2026-08-01 · `FJS-D74` — Custom service actions stay on `X-Service-Method` header dispatch.

**Status:** amended-by [`FJS-690`](ISSUES_ARCHIVE.md#fjs-690) — dispatch is a declared table now, not a block-list, so a method attached after construction 404s. That the header is the mechanism, that case is preserved and that CRUD is refused on it are unchanged.
Proposal to move to sub-path dispatch (`POST /api/notes/:id/summary`) was
considered and declined. Case is preserved for action names (`getStats` works);
CRUD names remain blocked from header override; `restore`/`upsert` match
case-insensitively.
*Lives in:* `packages/junction/src/transport/bridge.ts` (the header, the case rule and the CRUD refusal) · `packages/junction/src/core/service.ts` (the dispatch table `FJS-690` made authoritative).

### <a id="fjs-d75"></a>2026-08-01 · `FJS-D75` — `createService({ model })` carries the derived hook layer.
The model path must always include schema-derived gates/validation
(`base.hooks` = user hooks + derived); hook-less custom actions run the `'*'`
(all-hooks) pipeline, never an empty one. Litestone error names map across the
package boundary: `AccessDeniedError` → 403, `ValidationError` → 400.
*Lives in:* `packages/junction/src/core/service.ts`, `core/hooks.ts`,
`core/errors.ts`.

## UI substrate (Mesa)

### <a id="fjs-d1240"></a>2026-10-18 · `FJS-D1240` — Is a `_module.md` with front matter and no body a pass-through for the pages beneath it, and is one with a body and no `<slot />` refused at build — Split by body: a body-less `_module.md` is a pass-through, its front matter cascading to the pages beneath, which render unwrapped; a `_module.md` with a body and no `<slot />` is refused at build by name.

Asked in [`IDEAS/owed-rulings.md`](IDEAS/owed-rulings.md) § Open questions. **A** was picked over **B** (refuse every `_module.md` with no `<slot />`, body or not; `ksite port` writes the slot), **C** (pass-through for a body-less one only; a body with no slot keeps rendering empty).

The paper's recommendation, taken as written: the file with no body was written as data for its directory, which is what the legacy site did with it, and the one with a body and no slot is the silent empty `<main>` the row reports, so it is refused rather than guessed at.

### <a id="fjs-d1004"></a>2026-10-17 · `FJS-D1004` — How does a client's tag replace a template's of the same name in `autoImport`: a later directory wins, or an override is declared — The ordered list `markdownLayouts` already uses: a later `components` directory wins a name, and the conflict stays an error within ONE directory and between a directory and a `modules` binding. No new key and no new noun. Site-kit concatenates the engine's, the preset's and the site's `components` lists in that order, where today the site's replaces the preset's, and the build logs each override so an accidental shadow is still visible.

Asked in [`IDEAS/owed-rulings.md`](IDEAS/owed-rulings.md) § Open questions. **A** was picked over **B** (an explicit declaration: `autoImport: { components, overrides: ['content/blocks'] }`, where only a directory named there may take a name another already holds and every other duplicate still throws. Keeps the accidental-duplicate guard, but adds a second key that restates an order the `components` array already carries), **C** (A plus the page-local tier: a `_X.md` or `_X.mesa` beside a page is resolved for that page's subtree first, then the ordered list. Covers ksite's whole four-step resolver, but needs the importer to know which file it is injecting into and a scan per routes directory, which is a new scope concept in a plugin whose map is global today).

amended: the paper says site-kit already merges engine, preset and site autoImport in order, but config/vite.js reads siteConfig.autoImport ?? preset.sierra?.autoImport, so a site replaces the preset wholesale. A therefore also has site-kit concatenate the components lists engine, preset, site, and the build logs each override, since unplugin-vue-components' allowOverrides (the nearest precedent) overrides silently.

### <a id="fjs-d674"></a>2026-10-17 · `FJS-D674` — How does a relation picker add what tells repeated labels apart (`New · New · New · New request`): widen `@@label` to a column list, or a runtime `labelField` on `options()` / the Form — `@@label` takes a list whose parts are JOINED with ` · `, a null part dropped and never a first-non-null fallback (that stays `labelAlt`, the guessing tier), and an entry may be ONE hop through a to-one relation (`@@label([group.name, label])`): the parser checks the hop is to-one and the far column passes the one-entry rules, `options()` asks for the relation's column with the rows, a null relation (ELA's global steps, `groupId` null) drops its part, and a Search on that part is a relation filter. Two hops, a to-many, or a far column the far model's gate hides are refused at parse by name. `FJS-2130` (connectteam, `Employee` → `user.name`, filed 2026-10-09) is the same one hop and closes with it.

Asked in [`IDEAS/owed-rulings.md`](IDEAS/owed-rulings.md) § Open questions. **B** was picked over **A** (widen `@@label` to a list of OWN columns, per `FJS-D243`: litestone parses and checks each entry by the rules one entry has today, `x-label-field` carries the list, `labelFieldInfo` returns it, and `options()` joins the non-null parts with ` · ` (a Search matches any of them). One declaration, and every picker, ⌘K and detail line agrees. It solves neither measured case alone: ELA's desk is `TaskStatus.group` → `TaskGroup` via `groupId` (`fjs-prototypes/ela/db/schema.lite`), and a `@generated` column cannot read another table, so the desk name is not an own column there), **C** (`options(field, { labelField })` already exists as a single column; let it also take a function `(row) => string` (or a list of columns), and `<Form>` / `FormField` forward a per-field `labelField` prop. No schema change, but the answer lives in each screen, so the queue, the create form and ⌘K can disagree — the exact drift `labelFieldInfo` exists to prevent).

The paper's recommendation, taken as written: `FJS-D243` pre-decided the spelling (the existing noun widened) and the trigger has now come twice; both sightings, ELA's desk and connectteam's employee name, are one hop through a to-one relation, so A is a first cut that fixes neither, and the `@generated` fallback the earlier draft leaned on cannot cross a table. One hop with everything else refused at parse is the smallest rule that covers what was measured.

### <a id="fjs-d905"></a>2026-10-17 · `FJS-D905` — Who resets per-principal UI state when the session changes — Sierra emits a session-changed event (`session.onChange` or a DOM event on `document`) and `<Toaster>`, `<AlertProvider>` and `<CommandPalette>` subscribe and clear.

Asked in [`IDEAS/owed-rulings.md`](IDEAS/owed-rulings.md) § Open questions. **A** was picked over **B** (a `principal` prop on the providers; a change of value clears the store, and the app passes `session.user?.id`).

The paper's recommendation, taken as written: B is a prop every app must remember to pass, and forgetting it is silent, which is today's defect; A needs no caller and is the seam sierra already owes its own resource stores (`FJS-786`'s shape). It is an event on `document`, so ui imports nothing from sierra and Invariant 1 is untouched; its name is one new word and goes in `VOCABULARY.md`. Artefact: a drive that shows a toast, signs out and asserts the stack is empty.

### <a id="fjs-d1165"></a>2026-10-17 · `FJS-D1165` — What is a second, independent filtered list of one resource: a list that states its own `where` owning its rows, a documented `composed: true`, or a new option — A list that states `where` (or its own `query`) keeps its own rows, fed by its `load()` answer and kept live from pushes through `matchesQuery`; a list stating none stays the resource's store. `composed` keeps its meaning (includes). The doc line is one sentence: *a list over a filter is its own.*.

Asked in [`IDEAS/owed-rulings.md`](IDEAS/owed-rulings.md) § Open questions. **A** was picked over **B** (`composed: true` is the documented spelling for a second list, renamed or re-described as *own rows*, and `move()` learns to read the key from the list's rows. No schema or live-store change; the cost stays a full window re-read per announcement), **C** (docs only, the row's candidate: sierra's AGENTS.md says a list is its resource's store and names `composed: true` for a second one. Cheapest, and leaves the silent wrong-rows failure for the next app).

The paper's recommendation, taken as written: the failure is silent and fires on the natural spelling (jazzhr never meant to write two lists), so the default must be the safe one rather than a flag an app learns after it draws the wrong rows; B/C keep the trap and make every app pay a re-read per announcement.

### <a id="fjs-d1030"></a>2026-10-17 · `FJS-D1030` — What does a form control's `onchange` hand back: one shape for all, or a rule that sorts them (native control = DOM event, composite = value) — Two shapes with a stated rule: a control that IS a native element (`Input`, `Textarea`, `Select`, `CodeInput`) hands the DOM event; every composite hands its value. `Slider`/`NumberInput` drop `{ value }` for a bare number (a range stays `[start, end]`), so four shapes become two and the split follows what the control is. Each prop comment and the AGENTS table state the rule.

Asked in [`IDEAS/owed-rulings.md`](IDEAS/owed-rulings.md) § Open questions. **C** was picked over **A** (Every control's `onchange` receives the VALUE (`target.value`/`checked`/number/array/`[start, end]`), the event dropped. One handler shape; but `Input`'s event is what `e.target.files`, `e.target.form` and `FormField` read, and `oninput` would still be an event or need the same change), **B** (Every control's `onchange` receives `{ value, event }` (event absent for composites with no DOM event). One shape and nothing lost, at the price of every consumer destructuring, including the `Checkbox` that is `(on) => …` in AGENTS § Tables today), **D** (Change no code: put one line above each `onchange` prop comment and the AGENTS table naming the neighbours' shapes. Cheapest; a handler still fails on the neighbour, which is the row's complaint).

The paper's recommendation, taken as written: the split follows something a reader can see (is it a native element), it removes the only two shapes with no justification (`{ value }` object around one number, and `Checkbox` boolean vs Slider object), and it keeps `Input`'s event for the callers that need `files` and `form`; A and B reopen the 57 call sites for a gain C mostly gets.

### <a id="fjs-d1170"></a>2026-10-17 · `FJS-D1170` — When an autosave Form is destroyed inside its quiet window, does it send the waiting edit or warn that it dropped it — `onDestroy` flushes: if a timer is armed, send the write once more (fire and forget; `onautosaved` is not called on a destroyed form).

Asked in [`IDEAS/owed-rulings.md`](IDEAS/owed-rulings.md) § Open questions. **A** was picked over **B** (`onDestroy` drops the edit and `console.warn`s that a pending autosave was discarded, naming the model, so the screen owner calls `flushAutosave()`).

The paper's recommendation, taken as written: the quiet window exists so the person never presses save; losing the last edit on close is the one failure a form with no button cannot afford.

### <a id="fjs-d1078"></a>2026-10-16 · `FJS-D1078` — Which one event spelling does `.mesa` keep on an element — `onclick={fn}` everywhere, with `parseModifiers`' pipe grammar kept on the DOM name: `onsubmit|preventDefault={save}`, `oninput|debounce(300)={search}`. A guard modifier (`preventDefault`, `stopPropagation`, `self`, `trusted`, `debounce`, `throttle`) compiles into a wrapped handler VALUE, so it survives a spread and a kit component's forwarding — the reason Svelte 5 dropped modifier syntax. A listener option (`once`, `capture`, `passive`) cannot be a value, so it is honored on an element and refused on a component by name. `on:` and `@` refused with the new spelling.

Asked in [`IDEAS/lockdown.md`](IDEAS/lockdown.md) § Open questions. **C** was picked over **A** (`onclick={fn}` everywhere, elements and components alike; modifiers as an options object (`onclick={[fn, { once: true }]}` or a `use:` action); `on:` and `@` refused by name), **B** (`on:click` on elements (Svelte 4 habit, modifiers as `|once`), `onclick` on components as rule 23 says).

A drops modifiers, and the apps write about 234 of them, 202 of them preventDefault; C keeps the one spelling A wants and the grammar Mesa already has. The pipe stays over Vue's dot because a dot means a path everywhere else in the framework and arguments read cleanly after a pipe. Svelte 5's reason for dropping modifiers, a handler that travels as a value, is met by compiling the guard modifiers into the value and refusing the listener options on a component.

### <a id="fjs-d1139"></a>2026-10-16 · `FJS-D1139` — On `target: 'native'` every element carries one class for its tag, `_p` for a `<p>`, and a type selector naming a tag the target builds is lowered to it, in a component's `<style>` and a whole sheet alike; this replaces `FJS-D1088`'s scope-and-tag class.

Asked in chat while opening [`IDEAS/mesa-ir.md`](IDEAS/mesa-ir.md) § 12 step 4.5, through the question tool; the recommended answer was picked.

- **One class per tag, not one per scope and tag.** The kit's 63 type members (`.alert-content > strong`, `.field-group > label`) are global, so `.mHASH_p` could never serve them and an unscoped tag class was owed anyway. With it, `p.mHASH` is `._p.mHASH`: one class per element, one rewrite (`lowerTypes` in `native/css.js`), and `tagClass` in `native/tags.js` is the one spelling the runtime and the rewrite both read. Two classes per element, `.mHASH_p` beside `_p`, was the other option.
- **Specificity rises rather than falls.** A type is (0,0,1) and the class (0,1,0), so `p.mHASH` goes from (0,1,1) to (0,2,0) and still beats a single class, where `.mHASH_p` tied one. A global `strong` now ties a single-class rule it lost to, and the later rule wins.
- **The underscore is the kit's mark for private**, as in `--_fill`, and no class in the workspace starts with one.
- A tag the target has no element for (`dialog`, `summary`, `svg`, `html`, `body`) is still refused in a `<style>` and dropped from a sheet.

The nine were answered before the code. Q1/Q5: the class is derived from the tag the runtime built, and which tags lower from `NATIVE_TAGS`, so a new tag needs no edit. Q6: the rewrite sits beside `cssOffense` and is run by `scopeCSS` (the target's `lowerSelector`) and by `lowerSheet`. Q9: a runtime class and a rewrite that disagree would paint nothing in silence; one function names both, and the artefact is `none`, since no new test files are wanted while experimenting. Adjudication: *doctrine vs. discovery*, since `FJS-D1088` was ruled before the kit's own type selectors were measured. Tier: Register.

### <a id="fjs-d668"></a>2026-10-16 · `FJS-D668` — Should a named slot block (`slot="header"`) satisfy a component's snippet prop of the same name — The compiler owns it, and snippets are the one runtime system: `<h2 slot="header">…</h2>` lowers to `{#snippet header()}<h2>…</h2>{/snippet}`, and a component's `<slot name="header">fallback</slot>` lowers to `{@render header?.()}` with the fallback. `attachNamedSlotLegacy`, `makeSlots` and the slot runtime are deleted, along with Form's hand fallback; `slot=` carrying arguments is refused, naming the snippet form; a name that is neither slot nor prop keeps `FJS-926`'s warning. Markup with no arguments keeps the HTML spelling, and anything that takes data is a snippet. Added 2026-10-16 by lockdown 2.5, which widened this question to the whole of `FJS-2942`.

Asked in [`IDEAS/owed-rulings.md`](IDEAS/owed-rulings.md) § Open questions. **D** was picked over **A** (the `$slots` fallback Form has, copied into every component with a snippet prop. Each copy is a restatement of one rule, ~20 sites, and a new component forgets it), **B** (Mesa owns the translation: at construction, a block key that is not a declared slot but IS a declared prop of that name is delivered as the snippet prop (in `makeSlots`/`warnUnrenderableSlots`'s neighborhood; the compiler hands `makeSlots` the declared SLOT names today and would hand it the declared props too, the list `restProps` already receives). Then `Form`'s hand fallback is deleted and the warning keeps firing only for a name that is neither. Touches Mesa runtime semantics, so it wants a mesa test and the `ui` suite), **C** (warn only: keep `FJS-926` and sharpen its text to say "this component takes `header` as a snippet prop: `{#snippet header()}…{/snippet}`"; `slot=` stays a different protocol. No behavior change; Form's fallback stays the one exception).

B keeps two projection systems live in the runtime, which lockdown 2.5 exists to remove; D keeps the HTML spelling for markup with no arguments as compile-time sugar, so the runtime has one system (snippets) and the translation has one owner, the compiler. Familiarity vs. precision: the proven shape kept, an argument-carrying slot= refused by name.

### <a id="fjs-d1122"></a>2026-10-16 · `FJS-D1122` — The browser kit's page object is `tab` (`tab.online`, `tab.visible`, `tab.focused`), because sierra's router already exports `page`; `<mesa:window bind:online>` is removed, and the compiler refuses any `bind:` prop the runtime does not listen for.

Asked while building [`IDEAS/browser-kit.md`](IDEAS/browser-kit.md) 1.2, through the question tool, as two questions; the recommended answer was picked for each, the second after the owner asked what `bind:online` reports.

- **`tab`, not `page`.** `@frontierjs/sierra/router` exports `page` (`page.query`, `page.pathname`) and 294 files in this tree and the prototypes import it, so a route reading both would rename one with `as` — two nouns with one spelling in one app. `tab` names what the three facts are about. Its cost is stated: 27 files loop `as tab`, and inside such a loop the import is shadowed. `pageState` was refused because it reads as half of the router's object.
- **`bind:online` is removed, not rewired.** The plan had `bindWindow('online')` read the kit, but `runtime.js` importing `src/browser/` is a cycle, since the kit imports the runtime, and no app binds it — only mesa's own docs, its REPL example and the vscode completions did. `tab.online` is the one spelling. It reports `navigator.onLine`, the interface being up and not the server answering, which is why sierra's `pending.js` and `offline.js` arm on the socket's `connect` and read neither. The plan named `offline.js` as a second consumer, and that was wrong.
- **The compiler refuses a `bind:` prop outside `src/window-binds.js`**, which is the table the runtime listens by. Before this, an unknown prop compiled and was read once and never again, so a removed `bind:online` would have shown `undefined` and said nothing. The refusal is generic. It holds no special case for the old name (the evolution policy keeps nothing for an old spelling), and the REPL example was its first catch.

Adjudications: *familiarity vs. precision* for the noun — `page` is the platform's word (the Page Visibility API), and precision inside this framework wins, because the word is already taken here. Then *doctrine vs. discovery* for the plan's second consumer, which was amended to match the tree. Q9: the kit drive's `tab` spec flips each fact for real (network down, another tab in front), and `compiler.test.js` pins the refusal. The two questions were asked before any edit. The nine were answered late, after the drive was green, and all nine pass. Tier: Register.

### <a id="fjs-d1099"></a>2026-10-16 · `FJS-D1099` — css's breakpoint scale becomes a table in `vocabulary.js` that `breakpoint(name)` reads; the service worker is homestead's and the browser kit keeps only the push subscription; `fli check` warns on a hand-rolled `localStorage` or `document` keydown in an app that imports the kit.

Asked in [`IDEAS/browser-kit.md`](IDEAS/browser-kit.md) § Open questions (Q3, Q4, Q5), through the question tool, as three questions; the recommended answer was picked for each. With `FJS-D1097` this closes the paper's seven.

- **Q3 — a `breakpoints` table in `packages/css/vocabulary.js`, `{ sm: 640, md: 768, lg: 1024, xl: 1280, '2xl': 1536 }` in px.** The paper said css names no breakpoint; a probe found the scale already stated, but only in a `tokens.css` comment and as literals in `layout.css`, `facts.css` and `frame.css`. The comment becomes data: `breakpoint('md')` is `media('(min-width: 768px)')`, and the css spec that grades the vocabulary against the CSSOM grades every literal `@media` width in `src/` against the table. They stay literals in the CSS, for the reason `tokens.css` gives — a custom property cannot sit in a media query. A table in toolbelt was refused as a second home for a styling fact (Invariant 13); dropping `breakpoint()` leaves the apps' off-scale `47.99rem` ungraded.
- **Q4 — `homestead.md` owns service-worker registration and the precached shell; Phase 5 here keeps `pushSubscription()` → the notifications channel list.** The worker is release state and homestead already names it. Moving all of #10 there would lose the subscription's place beside the other wrappers, and owning the worker here would put two owners on one registration.
- **Q5 — a `warn` rule, scope `app`, that fires only when the app imports `@frontierjs/mesa/browser`.** The hand copy stays legal; the rule names the paved road once the road exists. The paper cited a `window.confirm` rule in `ui-hazards` as the precedent and none exists; the shape taken is `css-raw-literal`'s. An `error` was refused because storage that is not a preference and raw key handling in a canvas are legitimate.

The nine are the paper's, answered before the ruling; Q3's were re-answered late, after the probe moved its premise. Adjudications: *paved road vs. the workaround* for Q5, as the paper states it; *doctrine vs. discovery* for Q3's premise and Q5's precedent, both amended in the paper to match the tree. Q9 for Q3: an `@media` width off the table passes in silence today, and the vocabulary spec is the artefact once 1.4 lands. Tier: Register.

### <a id="fjs-d1097"></a>2026-10-16 · `FJS-D1097` — The browser kit is `@frontierjs/mesa/browser`, a subpath over one host-neutral primitive in `runtime.js`; a preference key carries sierra's `prefix`; a terminal call throws by name until a terminal app asks; an action returns `{ ok, via, reason }` and never throws for a missing API.

Asked in [`IDEAS/browser-kit.md`](IDEAS/browser-kit.md) § Open questions (Q1, Q2, Q6, Q7), through the question tool, as four questions; the recommended answer was picked for each. Q3–Q5 were ruled the same day in `FJS-D1099`.

- **Q1 — the home is a subpath, `src/browser/`, not a package.** Mesa is the leaf, so a package could not be consumed by `$$virtualEach` or `bindWindow`, which hold two of the private copies the kit removes; and the subpath is what mesa already does with a host or a tool (`/runtime/terminal`, `/runtime/native`, `/drive`, `/vite`). A `*-kit` package was priced: each of the three existing kits carries a dependency or a server half and this one has neither. **The trigger that moves it out is named** — a dependency, a server half, or a second host implementation `$$host` cannot carry. Folding into `/runtime` was refused because a terminal and a phone import that file.
- **Q2 — `persisted()` prefixes the key with sierra config's `prefix`, defaulting to the app's `package.json` name.** `example` already types `shop_theme` and `shop_token` by hand, which is the prefix with no owner; two apps on one dev origin (`FJS-740`) otherwise read each other's preferences. Set once by the router at boot, `''` without sierra.
- **Q6 — on a terminal or a phone a wrapper throws at its first call, by name.** A clock, a hotkey, a persisted value, focus and size each mean something in haven and `fli dev:tui`, and the names are chosen to port; but a storage or focus seam in `host/targets.js` with no consumer is a seam nothing tests. A silent default was refused by § V.9: a hotkey that never fires reports nothing. The rule is the one `{@attach}` already lives by there (`FJS-2242`).
- **Q7 — an action returns a `Result`.** `share()` that cannot share still copies and says `via: 'copy'`, so the caller shows *copied*; a throw puts the fallback branch back in every caller, which is the copy the kit exists to own.

The nine are answered in the paper, before any edit. Adjudications: *batteries vs. smallness* — zero dependencies, the core grows by one primitive; *coherence vs. convention* — the `*-kit` naming is the convention and the mesa subpath precedent is the nearer coherence; *familiarity vs. precision* — the field's names (`persisted`, `media`, `hotkey`) taken as is. Q9's artefact is one CDP spec per wrapper flipping the real condition, `none` until each lands. Tier: Register here; Map in `packages/mesa/CLAUDE.md` § Layout once Phase 0 lands.

### <a id="fjs-d1088"></a>2026-10-16 · `FJS-D1088` — A `<style>` rule a phone cannot paint refuses its file on `target: 'native'`, by selector and line, as a tag it lacks does; type selectors are lowered later, to a scope-and-tag class, rather than refused for good.

Asked in chat while closing [`IDEAS/mesa-ir.md`](IDEAS/mesa-ir.md) § 12 Phase 3, through the question tool, as two questions; the recommended answer was picked for each.

- **Refuse, not warn and drop.** `native/css.js` judges every prelude: type and attribute selectors, `@media`, `@supports`, `@layer`, `@container`, and the pseudo-classes §§ 9 and 11 found dropped. Warning and dropping the rule would let the 58 files it refuses compile, and a layout rule missing on a phone would then be visible only as a build warning. Refusing at one per-kind line was the third option, rejected because it is a second line to keep.
- **Type selectors are lowered in Phase 4 (4.5).** ~~Each element also carries a class naming its scope and tag, and `p.mHASH` is rewritten to `.mHASH_p`.~~ Amended 2026-10-16 by [`FJS-D1139`](#fjs-d1139): one class per tag, `p.mHASH` → `._p.mHASH`. Specificity falls from (0,1,1) to (0,1,0), which can reorder a tie against an unscoped single-class rule. Lowering them now, before Phase 3 closed, and refusing them for good were the other options.

The nine were answered after the code was written, and they are recorded as late. Q8 was the open one. Adjudication: *ergonomics vs. strictness*, where a phone painting a component half-styled costs more than a refusal naming the line. Q9: an unmeasured selector that paints nothing passes in silence (`none`), and the refusal path has no fixture. Tier: Register.

### <a id="fjs-d1074"></a>2026-10-15 · `FJS-D1074` — The Lynx backend is `target: 'native'`, read by the one emitter the terminal reads, and proved in mesa's `test` on Lynx for Web with the device run kept as a manual drive.

Asked in chat when `FJS-D1069`'s A started, through the question tool, as three questions; the recommended answer was picked for each.

- **The target is `'native'`, not `'lynx'`.** It names the medium, the way `'terminal'` does while OpenTUI stays inside `runtime-terminal.js`. Lynx is named only in `runtime-native.js`, so a second engine changes one file.
- **One emitter with a profile per target.** `terminal/emit.js` moves to a host-neutral path and reads a per-target profile: the tag table, the event table, whether the target paints CSS, and the runtime specifier. The emitted `$$tui` becomes `$$host` in both targets. A native bundle calling `$$tui` from a file under `terminal/` was the rejected alternative.
- **The drive is Lynx for Web in headless Chrome, in mesa's `test` script**, with the `@lynx-js/*` devDependencies pinned exact. The emulator sweep is a manual drive in `DRIVES.md`, because CI has no emulator. It is still owed per release, since web caught none of § 10's three device-only bugs.

Adjudication: *batteries vs. smallness*, as in `FJS-D1069`. Tier: Register. Plan: `IDEAS/mesa-ir.md` § 12.

### <a id="fjs-d1069"></a>2026-10-15 · `FJS-D1069` — FJS does not own Swift and Kotlin hosts. The spike's bundles run on a real Android device or emulator under Lynx Explorer first, and a Lynx backend is built in mesa only if native holds what Lynx for Web showed.

Asked in [`IDEAS/mesa-ir.md`](IDEAS/mesa-ir.md) § Open questions (`FJS-D689` step 5), through the question tool. **C, then A** was picked over **A** (build the Lynx backend now, without a device run) and **B** (build FJS hosts in Swift and Kotlin).

Research run before the ruling (`.cache/reports/Lynx versus own native hosts.md`, gitignored) found that every owned host with a published cost was carried by one large company for six to ten years, and that the hosts owned by a vendor, a consultancy or one person were retired or handed off. B buys nothing the spike measured, since the CSS layers, the missing controls and the async measure are FJS's on any host. The six ports to Lynx that are not React converged on the shape Mesa already emits: a background-thread tree, one batched op buffer per tick, and a fixed main-thread runtime replaying it through the Element PAPI. A device run comes first because § 9 ran on Lynx for Web, where a browser still does the cascade, inheritance and layout, and Lynx documents that its layout is not the web's. The Element PAPI carries no stability promise, so the backend talks to it through one runtime file, sits in mesa's own CI, and pins an exact engine version. A binding kept beside its host died with Svelte Native. **If native parity collapses, the answer is *not Lynx yet*, never *own hosts*.**
The nine are the paper's, under the question; they were answered before the ruling, and checked again after it was written. Adjudication: *batteries vs. smallness*, because Lynx stays severable behind one runtime file. Tier: Register.
— `IDEAS/mesa-ir.md` § 6 step 4.

### <a id="fjs-d1042"></a>2026-10-15 · `FJS-D1042` — How does a `sierra.config.js` say *the page's own origin* for `junction.url`, now that `FJS-D552` evaluates it in Node — The page decides: `virtual:sierra` emits `url: import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL || location.origin`, and `junction.url` in the config is the answer where there is no page (the terminal shell, a prerender) and what turns the client on. Asked in [`IDEAS/owed-rulings.md`](IDEAS/owed-rulings.md) § Open questions. **A** was picked over **B** (a path-only `url` (`'/'`) means the page's origin, resolved by the client against `location`. One key, one meaning; the terminal then needs an absolute URL from `--api` and refuses a relative one by name, so `bun run tui`, `fli dev:tui` and `verify-tui` all change).

The paper's recommendation, taken as written: every config in the tree already meant *the page's origin in a browser, this port elsewhere*, and `VITE_API_URL` is already the one override every surface's build reads; A moves that sentence into the one place that runs in the page. ### <a id="fjs-d552"></a>2026-10-15 · `FJS-D552` — How does `virtual:sierra` hand `junction`, `analytics` and `theme` to the browser without importing `sierra.config.js` whole, when a custom analytics provider holds functions — Emit the three keys by value (`JSON.stringify`), and refuse a function anywhere in them at config load, naming the key path. Asked in [`IDEAS/owed-rulings.md`](IDEAS/owed-rulings.md) § Open questions. **A** was picked over **B** (a separate client-side config file (`config/sierra.client.js`) holding the browser keys, which `virtual:sierra` imports instead. It is a second origin for one config and a new file noun), **C** (emit by value when the three keys are pure data, and fall back to the whole import when a function is present. That leaves two mechanisms, and the fallback silently brings the defect back for any app with a custom provider).

The paper's recommendation, taken as written: the config stays the one origin, and a function the browser cannot receive is refused by name instead of dropped. Only one README shape changes, and nothing in the tree uses it.

### <a id="fjs-d904"></a>2026-10-15 · `FJS-D904` — Who owns where a kit overlay mounts, and which overlay answers Escape — One helper in `utils.js`, `overlayHost()` = the topmost `dialog:modal`, else `body`, which every portal calls; plus a rule that an overlay answering Escape calls `preventDefault()`, graded by a drive.

The paper's recommendation, taken as written: one owner for one question; B is two answers, and the top layer's stacking order against a later `showModal()` is a second thing to learn. The owner already exists: ConfirmPanel's `host()` (`ConfirmPanel.mesa` L42) is promoted to `utils.js`, not written a second time. ### <a id="fjs-d903"></a>2026-10-15 · `FJS-D903` — What owns "a field changed" in a `<Form>` — `$context.form.changed(name)`: every control calls it on commit, `writeField` calls it, and it is the one place that sets `dirty`, retires `_server` and arms autosave; `handleChange` becomes a caller of it.

The paper's recommendation, taken as written: B makes six controls fake a DOM event to reach a function in the same component tree, and a click-committed value has no element to be honest about; A is Invariant 4's shape (add to the owner) and a control outside a form calls nothing. ### <a id="fjs-d979"></a>2026-10-14 · `FJS-D979` — Q4 — A box that hides what is under it — One opaque treatment lowered in `runtime-terminal.js`, so no color is written in a `.mesa`.

Asked in [`IDEAS/haven.md`](IDEAS/haven.md) § Open questions. **B** was picked over **A** (leave it to the app, the same attach helper as Q3).

The paper's recommendation, taken as written: every dialog and dropdown on a terminal needs it, and a color in a `.mesa` is Invariant 13's failure.

A browser and a terminal then agree on which boxes hide what is under them, and an app writes the class it already writes. `glass` is the one divergence: translucent in a browser, opaque on a terminal, which has no half-covered cell. Mesa is a leaf and cannot import the stylesheet, so `src/terminal/tags.js` holds the two lists and `test/terminal-tags.test.js` holds them to `surface.css`; a `class:` naming one of them toggles it as the attribute does. ### <a id="fjs-d972"></a>2026-10-14 · `FJS-D972` — Q3 — Which layouts ship in Phase 2 — `sidebar`, `rail` and `topbar`. The topbar draws `groups` flat, and portal's More menu stays out.

Asked in [`IDEAS/app-shell.md`](IDEAS/app-shell.md) § Open questions. **B** was picked over **A** (`sidebar` and `rail` only. The topbar apps keep their own `_module.mesa` over `ui/nav`).

### <a id="fjs-d987"></a>2026-10-13 · `FJS-D987` — The terminal shell's keys are modal — Focus sets the mode: a text field is INSERT and takes every key but Esc; anywhere else, or a field after Esc, is NORMAL, where h j k l are the arrows, a j or k the page leaves alone moves focus, `i` types into the field again, and a letter types nothing. The mode line sits in a footer under the page.

Picked by the owner over **vim proper** (start NORMAL everywhere, `i` or Enter to type), **list screen only**, and **later**. Auto-insert costs no key before typing and keeps every drive that types into a field working unchanged; what it gives up is j and k leaving a field without an Esc or a Tab first.

**The mode is Sierra's shell's, not Mesa's runtime's.** The runtime delivers keys as a browser does (`FJS-D809`), and a browser has no modes. What the runtime added is what a DOM handler already reads — `tagName`, and `type` on an input — and `footerOf(renderer)`, a strip beside the scrolling page, because a mode line at the top scrolls away on any list taller than the screen. **Esc out of INSERT is stopped at the window**, so a dialog closes and the shell goes back on the second Esc, not the first. **The arrows stay the route's**: a Haven scene walks on them, so the shell moves focus with them only between its own list buttons. **h j k l are renamed to the arrows before the runtime makes a keydown of them**, in a key listener `shell.js` adds ahead of the first mount, so a route reading arrows walks on vim's keys without knowing a mode exists, and the browser, which has none, is untouched. A route that acts on an arrow prevents it; that is what tells the shell a j was a step and not a move of focus.
*Lives in:* `packages/sierra/src/terminal/Shell.mesa` (the keys), `shell.js` (h j k l as the arrows, and j or k moving focus), `Mode.mesa` (the line), `packages/mesa/src/runtime-terminal.js` (`footerOf`, `tagName`). *Proved by:* `example/web/test/verify-tui.mjs` (the modes), `packages/haven/web/test/verify-explore.mjs` (h j k l walking), `packages/mesa/test/terminal/specs/footer.spec.mjs` (the footer, `tagName`, `type`).

### <a id="fjs-d672"></a>2026-10-13 · `FJS-D672` — Who sorts when a `<Table>` has no `onsort`: the Table locally, the caller only, or an explicit opt-in — The Table sorts locally when no `onsort` is stated: it owns the sort, so `rows` reach the row snippet ordered by `orderBy`. `onsort` stays the "the sort lives elsewhere (URL, server)" switch. A caller that sorts server-side behind `bind:orderBy` is sorted a second time, harmlessly for a stable sort on the same key. The comparator is a fact with one owner, `comparatorFor`/`compareValues` in junction's `query-values.ts`; `@frontierjs/ui` depends on toolbelt only, so that comparator would have to move down to `@frontierjs/toolbelt/query` first. The case it gets wrong in silence is a Table over ONE PAGE of a server list with no `onsort` (basecamp's `apps/index.mesa` and `deployments/index.mesa` pass `rows={list.rows}` and no `onsort`): it sorts the page, not the list. The switch already exists, `onsort={list.sort}` (ELA's `forms`, `actions`, `integrations` screens), so a list handle's Table states it.

Asked in [`IDEAS/owed-rulings.md`](IDEAS/owed-rulings.md) § Open questions. **A** was picked over **B** (the affordance needs `onsort`: no `onsort`, no button, whatever the column says. `bind:orderBy` retires (the Table never owns the sort, it only states the move), the `orderBy = next` branch is deleted, and the datatable spec's bound-sort cases move to `onsort`. Smallest change, but every local-data table has to hand-write the sort that `columns()` already promised), **C** (an explicit opt-in prop (`sort="local"`) beside `onsort`. Honest, but a new option on a component whose default is the broken case, and `columns()` still marks everything sortable).

The paper's recommendation, with its one silent case closed in the same change: basecamp's `apps/index.mesa` and `deployments/index.mesa` pass one page of a server list with no `onsort`, so they bind `onsort={list.sort}` when the Table starts sorting locally. Otherwise those two screens would sort the page rather than the list.

### <a id="fjs-d959"></a>2026-10-13 · `FJS-D959` — Does a child component's await or throw reach its parent's boundary — The nearest ancestor boundary at runtime, across component edges (Svelte).

Asked in [`IDEAS/derived-suspense.md`](IDEAS/derived-suspense.md) § Open questions. **B** was picked over **A** (component-local).

The paper's recommendation, taken as written: it is what makes one hand-placed boundary per page region enough, which is most of what derivation promised. `captureContext()` already carries context across the edge.

### <a id="fjs-d958"></a>2026-10-13 · `FJS-D958` — Does an update that changes several async values tear — Synchronized: every region reading a value the update re-awaits keeps its old content until all of them settle, then commits once (Svelte).

Asked in [`IDEAS/derived-suspense.md`](IDEAS/derived-suspense.md) § Open questions. **B** was picked over **A** (per-value commit).

The paper's recommendation, taken as written: as its own item ahead of any placement work. It is the tearing fix and it holds whoever places the boundary. It costs a batch in the runtime's scheduler, which is internal and adds no user-facing noun.

### <a id="fjs-d957"></a>2026-10-13 · `FJS-D957` — What does an await with no boundary around it do — The await holds its nearest ancestor boundary, else the component, until it settles (Svelte).

Asked in [`IDEAS/derived-suspense.md`](IDEAS/derived-suspense.md) § Open questions. **B** was picked over **A** (keep that, and make derived placement purely additive), **C** (derive a boundary for it (this paper's idea)).

The paper's recommendation, taken as written: and C only once a real screen wants finer reveal than hand placement gives. B closes the `undefined` flash with no new concept. C is then an optimization over B, and the next three questions are its price.

### <a id="fjs-d956"></a>2026-10-13 · `FJS-D956` — Where does a failure go — A failure bubbles to the nearest boundary that has `failed`, else to the component root and the console, and `failed` receives `reset`.

Asked in [`IDEAS/derived-suspense.md`](IDEAS/derived-suspense.md) § Open questions. **B** was picked over **A** (`failed` placed with `pending`).

The paper's recommendation, taken as written: an error region usually wants to be coarser than a loading one, and a swallowed error is the silence § V's ninth question exists to refuse.

### <a id="fjs-d667"></a>2026-10-13 · `FJS-D667` — How does the compiler tell a resource handle's destructure from a meant snapshot — A runtime check: the destructure expansion, in dev builds only, reads the source's property descriptors and warns once when a destructured key is an accessor. The shape is a fact at runtime, so nothing is declared and a meant snapshot over a plain object stays quiet.

Asked in [`IDEAS/owed-rulings.md`](IDEAS/owed-rulings.md) § Open questions. **A** was picked over **B** (the handle declares itself: `createResource`'s handle carries a marker (a symbol), and the same runtime check keys on it. Cheaper than A but a hand-rolled handle is not covered), **C** (warn on every top-level destructure of a call result and give a meant snapshot another spelling (`untrack(() => …)` or `snapshot()`); this retires FJS-1969's quiet spelling and adds a noun).

The paper's recommendation, taken as written: the compiler lacks the shape and the runtime has it, which is derive-instead-of-declare; it adds no noun and no option, and a wrong destructure becomes a dev-time warning rather than silence. Under every option the expansion must evaluate the call ONCE: probed 2026-10-09, `const { rows, loading } = r.list()` emits `const rows = r.list().rows; const loading = r.list().loading` and `const { port, host } = load()` calls `load()` twice, so `loading` reads a second handle (a second fetch) and not `rows`'s. A's check reads its descriptors off the one temporary that fix introduces.

### <a id="fjs-d954"></a>2026-10-13 · `FJS-D954` — Q2 — How does a page opt out of the frame — `reset: true` on the page, and Sierra makes it reach every page under a `_module.mesa` that declares it — a few lines in `parseRouteFile`. It is what a reader predicts, since every other layout frontmatter key reaches the pages beneath; it is also unsettled whether the declaring layout itself still renders, and no caller exists to settle it.

Asked in [`IDEAS/app-shell.md`](IDEAS/app-shell.md) § Open questions. **B** was picked over **A** (`reset: true` on the page, and Sierra REFUSES it on a `_module.mesa` by name rather than dropping it. A bare directory is one line per page), **C** (a `bare` list of prefixes in `nav.js`, as four shells do today).

what a reader predicts: every other _module.mesa frontmatter key reaches the pages beneath it, and reset alone does not. Picked for now, ahead of a second bare page under one directory.

### <a id="fjs-d946"></a>2026-10-13 · `FJS-D946` — If B: how does a module-block signal cross an import — An exported reactive value is refused by name; only functions export. Half 1 is then the whole feature, and pillar 1 stays mixed across files.

Asked in [`IDEAS/review-solid-octane.md`](IDEAS/review-solid-octane.md) § Open questions. **C** was picked over **A** (An exported reactive value is emitted as an accessor function, and an importer writes `canEdit()`. The template already tracks it; RULE 2 grows one case: a `const` calling an import from a `.mesa` file can move. It costs a name spelled `x` in its own file and `x()` everywhere else), **B** (The compiler reads the imported `.mesa` file's module block and learns which exports are signals: the `externalSignals` map, derived instead of written, which retires the drift that map was criticized for. It needs the Vite plugin to hand the compiler a resolver. A barrel re-export is blind to it, so a re-exported `.mesa` name needs a warning).

follows from RULE 51 standing (A): a module block exports functions only, and an exported reactive value is refused by name so the attempt is loud rather than a value that silently stops tracking.

### <a id="fjs-d371"></a>2026-10-13 · `FJS-D371` — Does RULE 51 stand: must derived state live in a component — RULE 51 stands. A derivation shared by two components is computed at the write site; the chain above is written as a function of the store and called in each component.

Asked in [`IDEAS/review-solid-octane.md`](IDEAS/review-solid-octane.md) § Open questions. **A** was picked over **B** (`<script module>` gets the instance script's semantics: a top-level `let` is a signal and a `const` that reaches one re-derives, once per module rather than per instance. RULE 51 narrows to plain `.js` files), **C** (RULE 51 is withdrawn: `createMemo` in a `.js` module is blessed and documented as the way to share a derivation).

derivation keeps one home, the component, where an owner disposes it; a module-scope signal never disposes, and a derivation two components share is a plain function of the store called in each.

### <a id="fjs-d671"></a>2026-10-12 · `FJS-D671` — Where does a list's selection live: a standalone set primitive the screen composes, a Table-owned column, or a resource-owned set — A standalone signal-backed primitive in `@frontierjs/ui` (a `.js` module beside `dnd.js`): `createSelection(keyOf)` with `has(row)`, `toggle(row)`, `clear()`, `set(rows)`, `count`, and `stateOf(rows)` returning `none | some | all`; plus `Checkbox` `indeterminate` and a `<BulkBar {selection}>` that shows the count and a slot for the actions. The screen draws the header box through `header(col)` and the row box in its own snippet. No change to `Table`.

Asked in [`IDEAS/owed-rulings.md`](IDEAS/owed-rulings.md) § Open questions. **A** was picked over **B** (`Table` owns it: `selectable` and `bind:selected` draw a leading select column, the header tri-state box, and hand the row snippet a `selected` flag. Fewest lines in a screen, but the table must draw a cell inside a `<tr>` the caller wrote, which breaks the contract `row` has today), **C** (the resource owns it: `resource.selection` in sierra's `createResource`, so the set survives paging, filtering and live-store updates and names ids rather than rows. Right for ELA's inbox, but it makes UI-kit selection depend on sierra, and a list not backed by a resource has nowhere to put one).

The paper's recommendation, taken as written: it is the smallest piece that deletes the hand-rolled Set, bar and `.indeterminate` effect, it adds no coupling, and C can wrap it later (a resource handing out a `createSelection` keyed by primary key) without changing it. The sighting rules C out as the first piece anyway: ELA's inbox selects messages AND tickets in one column (`FJS-2003`), two resources, so a resource-owned set cannot hold that one selection, while `keyOf` can key it by kind and id.

### <a id="fjs-d895"></a>2026-10-10 · `FJS-D895` — A pointer or wheel gesture has no terminal lowering, and a component states nothing about the surfaces it reaches: the refusal is the statement.

Asked in [`IDEAS/mesa-ir.md`](IDEAS/mesa-ir.md) slices 29 and 30, where `/automations/flows/:flowId/` stopped at FlowCanvas's `on:pointerdown`. The owner picked **A** (the canvas stays off the terminal) over **B** (a terminal form of a flow, the nodes and links as text) and **C** (lower pointer and wheel to the terminal's mouse reports). C draws nothing to drag, since an svg paints its label or nothing. The route stays refused, and `fli dev:tui --list` naming `on:pointerdown` is the reason a reader needs.

**A declaration was proposed and cut.** A component saying it has no terminal form would state a second time what the refusal already names (§ V *origin*, *derived*), add a noun (*concept*), and could hide a route that lowers with nothing saying so (*silence*). "Browser-only" is the wrong word too: on a phone a pointer event is a touch, and `FJS-D692` cuts the gesture set from the terminal's table and the phone's together. B is not refused: a flow drawn as text is a terminal form a later slice may build.

**§ V.** *Origin*: `TERMINAL_EVENTS` (`packages/mesa/src/terminal/tags.js`), which already owns what the terminal lowers. *Concept*: none. *Complexity*: the problem's, since a terminal has no canvas. *Predictability*: unchanged; an event outside the table is refused as every other is. *Derived*: the route's refusal is derived from the component. *Owner*: the table. *Boundary*: the refusal names file and line. *Failure*: a refusal, as a gesture a reader could not make would otherwise be a dead control. *Silence*: that a pointer or wheel handler is refused for the terminal; `terminal-emit.test.js` *a pointer or wheel gesture* fails if one enters the table.

### <a id="fjs-d894"></a>2026-10-10 · `FJS-D894` — On the terminal a file input is a field a path is typed into; a hidden one opens in place on `click()`.

Asked in [`IDEAS/mesa-ir.md`](IDEAS/mesa-ir.md) slice 30, where `/stocktake/` stopped at a file input on screen. The owner picked **A** (a path field) over **B** (keep refusing it) and **C** (paint it inert). C drops a control a reader needed with nothing said, the trade slice 16 already refused for an unlabeled svg (*ergonomics vs. strictness*).

Committing the field, by Enter or by leaving it, reads the file into `files` and fires `input` then `change`, as a browser does when its picker closes on a new choice. `value` is the browser's `C:\fakepath\` plus the name. A path that reads no file leaves the choice as it was and says `no file at <path>` in the emptied field. One hidden by a static or live `hidden` or `visually-hidden` paints nothing until `click()`, the call the kit's `FileUpload` makes from its button: then it shows in place, and Enter or leaving it hides it and hands focus back. A bind on a file input stays refused.

**§ V, answered after the edit, so late.** *Origin*: one row in `INPUT_TYPES` and one class, `FilePath`. *Concept*: none; it is the text field the terminal already has. *Complexity*: the problem's, since a terminal has no picker. *Predictability*: `files`, `value` and the event order are a browser's. *Derived*: whether one paints is `pickerHidden`, read on every `hidden` or `class` write. *Owner*: the terminal runtime's `element()` and `set_attribute`. *Boundary*: `files` holds real `File`s. *Failure*: a bad path is said in the field rather than thrown. *Silence*: that a committed path reaches `files` and `change`, and a hidden one opens on `click()`; `test/terminal/specs/files.spec.mjs` fails when either stops.

### <a id="fjs-d856"></a>2026-10-10 · `FJS-D856` — Is `part:` the spelling — `part="header"` on the child, `part:header="dense"` on the parent.

Asked in [`IDEAS/child-part-styling.md`](IDEAS/child-part-styling.md) § Open questions. **A** was picked over **B** (custom properties per styled property, the DatePicker shape), **C** (a prop map, `parts={{ header: 'dense' }}`, as Tailwind-ish kits pass a class string per slot).

The paper's recommendation, taken as written: the platform's word with the platform's meaning, so the shape is stolen whole (*familiarity vs. precision*). B is what `FJS-128` walked away from, and C is a runtime object the compiler cannot see, which leaves question 2's parent-scoped resolution nowhere to happen.

### <a id="fjs-d838"></a>2026-10-09 · `FJS-D838` — A preview build has no `data-fjs-loc` — A preview build stamps `data-fjs-loc`, behind a named `site-kit build --preview` mode that production cannot reach by default.

Asked in [`IDEAS/anchored-feedback.md`](IDEAS/anchored-feedback.md) § Open questions. **A** was picked over **B** (the anchor stores a selector and a quote, and the dev server maps it to a `loc` at handoff).

The paper's recommendation, taken as written: the handoff is the payoff, and a selector is the anchor Pinmark shows drifting. Leaking source paths is acceptable on a link handed to a reviewer and not in production, which is what the named mode and a `dist/` check for an absent panel are for.

### <a id="fjs-d836"></a>2026-10-09 · `FJS-D836` — Is `sierra` a reader or does the page-level kind go somewhere else — Sierra emits the shell-level facts itself (`lang` on `<html>`, the skip link to `<main>`), and landmarks and heading order are asserted by the browser drive on rendered pages.

Asked in [`IDEAS/accessibility.md`](IDEAS/accessibility.md) § Open questions. **C** was picked over **A** (sierra is a reader: the prerender tap that grades a route's reads against `@@gate` also grades its landmarks, heading order and skip link, and fails the build), **B** (a `fli check` rule over the app's layout and route files, at review).

The paper's recommendation, taken as written: `lang` and the skip link are facts sierra can write rather than check, which is the derive-instead-of-restate answer. Landmarks and heading order exist only in rendered output: A sees the prerendered routes and none of the SPA ones, and B reads source text that a layout chain and `{#if}` rearrange, so both would pass routes they never saw.

### <a id="fjs-d821"></a>2026-10-09 · `FJS-D821` — Server-side render for prerendered pages vs — The same function at prerender and in the browser.

Asked in [`IDEAS/markdown-kit.md`](IDEAS/markdown-kit.md) § Open questions. **B** was picked over **A** (client-only: `Cell` renders the markdown in the browser).

The paper's recommendation, taken as written: a prerendered careers page that shows `## About the role` until hydration is the defect that found this. B costs nothing once the renderer is the pure function the first question recommends.

### <a id="fjs-d816"></a>2026-10-09 · `FJS-D816` — Where does the incubating print-kit land, what is it called, and what should have moved it — `packages/print-kit` as `@frontierjs/print-kit`, now; and an incubating piece exits when a SECOND app imports it, not when a first-party app does.

Asked by `fjs-prototypes/transit/PLAN.md` § Scope, which reserved the name for `decision-rules` at move time. **A** (`print-kit`, the `<output>-kit` spelling beside `email-kit`, npm name matching the directory as `FJS-D15` set) was picked over **B** (`pdf-kit` — the kit also answers a PNG, so the narrower name lies) and **C** (`printer` — collides with `app.printer`, the claim, and names the object rather than the kit).

**The trigger was the wrong proxy.** It named a first-party consumer (`example` or `basecamp` sends a PDF) as the sign a piece is framework; neither did, and meanwhile lago imported the kit by relative path across two prototype trees, serpgrid Q9 planned on it and sstime deferred a PDF export. Three outside consumers is the signal; *a first-party app uses it* is one kind of that signal and not the only one. The rule, for every piece incubating in a prototype from here: **it moves when a second app imports it**, whichever app that is, and a path import across `fjs-prototypes/` trees is the defect that forces the move the same day ([`FJS-2229`](ISSUES.md#fjs-2229)). Invariant 1 holds: the kit imports `@frontierjs/mesa/drive` and nothing from junction; it is not a battery, as Q7 ruled.

*Lives in:* `packages/print-kit/`. *Resolves:* transit PLAN Q7's exit. *Adjudication:* batteries vs. smallness (§ IV). *Enforced by:* none — no rule yet refuses a path import across `fjs-prototypes/` trees; the hearing ran after the edit.

### <a id="fjs-d815"></a>2026-10-09 · `FJS-D815` — How fine is a derived boundary — The lowest node, but boundaries in one component reveal together.

Asked in [`IDEAS/derived-suspense.md`](IDEAS/derived-suspense.md) § Open questions. **B** was picked over **A** (the lowest node per value, as § *The idea* states), **C** (the component root: derive the watch set, never the placement).

The paper's recommendation, taken as written: if placement is derived at all (the first question's C, which it recommends only later). A gives the pending region the data region's exact shape, and a page whose regions pop in one at a time, shifting layout at each arrival. That is right about correctness and wrong about what a person sees.

### <a id="fjs-d810"></a>2026-10-09 · `FJS-D810` — Does § 8's "TUI: not before core leaves alpha" still hold — Amend § 8 to admit the shell now, as a stressor: `example/web` run in a terminal, read-only routes first.

Asked in [`IDEAS/terminal-surface.md`](IDEAS/terminal-surface.md) § Open questions. **B** was picked over **A** (amend § 8 to stop at components: the target keeps growing as the IR's consumer, and an app shell waits for core to leave alpha), **C** (hold the line, and stop terminal work at what exists).

The paper's recommendation, taken as written: the example app is the corpus that grades the IR, and a shell turns the portability report's count into screens a person can open. Read-only first, because the form path (`bind:` on a component, `on:submit`) is the widest remaining blocker.

### <a id="fjs-d809"></a>2026-10-09 · `FJS-D809` — Where does the terminal version of an app live — A target of `web/`: Sierra builds the same `web/src/routes` with `target: 'terminal'` into a shell that lists the routes and mounts one, and `fli dev:tui` runs it. No new directory; a route that does not lower says so by name.

Asked in [`IDEAS/terminal-surface.md`](IDEAS/terminal-surface.md) § Open questions. **C** was picked over **A** (a new `tui/` surface beside `web/`, with its own config, port slot, `fli dev:tui` and release. Amends Invariant 3), **B** (a mode of `cli/`: the same binary, config (origin, tenant) and release that `FJS-D397` gave commands, with a screen mode beside them).

The paper's recommendation, taken as written: the ask is the same app painted by another backend, and `FJS-D38` rules that a surface is a compiler backend, never a second way to write a component. A and B each start a second route tree. Shipping a terminal app to users as a binary is `cli/`'s release, and is a question for after something runs.

### <a id="fjs-d808"></a>2026-10-09 · `FJS-D808` — Is the parent-scoped-class resolution in v1 — Design-system classes only in v1; `:global()` stays for a bespoke rule.

Asked in [`IDEAS/child-part-styling.md`](IDEAS/child-part-styling.md) § Open questions. **A** was picked over **B** (v1 includes resolving `part:header="tight"` to `tight mHASHp` at the parent, through `resolveAsNode`).

The paper's recommendation, taken as written: then B once a second `:global()` reaches into a child. The demand is one use in the repo, and Invariant 13 already says a parent styles with a tone and a treatment, which A covers whole.

### <a id="fjs-d806"></a>2026-10-09 · `FJS-D806` — Whether `<Form>`'s existing answer is the model for the rest — Yes: each component asks a context at the point of use what it owes, the way a control asks `$context.form`, and the kit holds only what no context can answer.

Asked in [`IDEAS/accessibility.md`](IDEAS/accessibility.md) § Open questions. **A** was picked over **B** (no: the kit is a full table for every term, and `<Form>` becomes one more reader of it).

The paper's recommendation, taken as written: then the table only for what is left. Build one behavioral component (Dialog's focus trap and labelled title) the `<Form>` way first and price the kit against what remains; *cut one level simpler* says not to tabulate the kind that already derives.

### <a id="fjs-d673"></a>2026-10-09 · `FJS-D673` — Does a plain multi-line String (an address, a note) get a schema word now, or wait for a sighting — `@syntax(txt)`: plain text's file extension beside `md`, the catalog's own rule for the argument; `x-syntax: txt` → `textarea` with plain display in `displayFor` (no Markdown rendering). No new attribute, and a natural language is a syntax too. It redefines an existing answer rather than adding one: probed 2026-10-09, `controlFor({ type: 'string', 'x-syntax': 'text' })` answers `{ control: 'code', language: 'text' }` today, an unhighlighted code editor that falls through rather than a designed answer.

Asked in [`IDEAS/owed-rulings.md`](IDEAS/owed-rulings.md) § Open questions. **B** was picked over **A** (wait: close the row's residue until an app declares a column that needs it, then the sighting names the shape. No code, no noun), **C** (derive from `@length`: a `maxLength` above a threshold (say 200) is `textarea`. No new word, but a magic number, and a column that is long and one-line (a URL) is misdrawn).

The case is already in the tree: example's note String @length(0, 500) draws one line and strips a pasted newline, so waiting buys nothing. txt is plain text's file extension, which is the catalog's rule for @syntax's argument, so prose gets the textarea md already gets without a new attribute or a magic length. The fall-through answer it replaces (an unhighlighted code editor) has no users; pre-alpha it is redefined, not preserved.

### <a id="fjs-d726"></a>2026-10-09 · `FJS-D726` — Does the derivation want to be visible — A `--explain` listing what was placed where, the same reporting surface item 5 of `IDEAS/static-safety.md` wants.

Asked in [`IDEAS/derived-suspense.md`](IDEAS/derived-suspense.md) § Open questions. **B** was picked over **A** (silent).

The paper's recommendation, taken as written: a compiler whose output differs from the source owes a report of the difference, and one reporting surface already wanted by `static-safety.md` costs less than a second. Moot unless derived placement is built.

### <a id="fjs-d725"></a>2026-10-09 · `FJS-D725` — Interaction with `{#virtual each}` — Nothing special: a `{#virtual each}` over an awaited list is a region like any other, held by its boundary until the list settles, then it renders its first window; on the server the SSR answer awaits it.

Asked in [`IDEAS/derived-suspense.md`](IDEAS/derived-suspense.md) § Open questions. **A** was picked over **B** (the block is its own boundary, and before the list arrives it renders a window of placeholder rows sized from the row height).

The paper's recommendation, taken as written: B is a skeleton derived from the markup, which the fallback question above turns down in favor of an authored `pending`. Under the SSR answer's B the server awaits the list and renders the first real window, which is the case `FJS-067` was about.

### <a id="fjs-d724"></a>2026-10-09 · `FJS-D724` — Does a value read only in an attribute get its own boundary — Attribute reads bubble to the element's parent.

Asked in [`IDEAS/derived-suspense.md`](IDEAS/derived-suspense.md) § Open questions. **A** was picked over **B** (their own boundary).

The paper's recommendation, taken as written: an image gated alone reads as a broken layout, and its parent is the smallest region a person reads as one thing.

### <a id="fjs-d723"></a>2026-10-09 · `FJS-D723` — Where does a derived boundary's fallback come from — The nearest `pending` snippet in scope, walking up (build step 3).

Asked in [`IDEAS/derived-suspense.md`](IDEAS/derived-suspense.md) § Open questions. **A** was picked over **B** (a blank region), **C** (a skeleton derived from the gated markup).

The paper's recommendation, taken as written: and read it as evidence for B in the first question. Once the fallback has to be authored, placing the snippet is placing the boundary in all but name, and the derivation saves one wrapper element.

### <a id="fjs-d700"></a>2026-10-09 · `FJS-D700` — Does the IR carry raw HTML tag names, or only the abstract vocabulary — Raw tags plus a per-target lowering table. Every existing component compiles, and portability is whatever the table covers.

Asked in [`IDEAS/mesa-ir.md`](IDEAS/mesa-ir.md) § Open questions. **A** was picked over **B** (abstract vocabulary only, with raw tags as a web-only escape node. Cleaner, but every raw `<div>` in the corpus becomes an escape).

### <a id="fjs-d699"></a>2026-10-09 · `FJS-D699` — Where do the terminal emitter and its runtime live — In `@frontierjs/mesa`: the emitter is a stage of `compiler.js` selected by a target option, the runtime is a sibling of `runtime.js` exported at a subpath, and the engine is an optional peer, as happy-dom already is.

Asked in [`IDEAS/mesa-ir.md`](IDEAS/mesa-ir.md) § Open questions. **A** was picked over **B** (a new package, `@frontierjs/mesa-terminal`, that imports the compiler's IR and holds the emitter and runtime).

The paper's recommendation, taken as written: § 7's sixth answer already places lowering inside the one compiler, and B would make the IR a published interface before it has two consumers. The `cli/` surface (Invariant 3) is where an app would run the output, and that is a separate question for after the first slice.

### <a id="fjs-d698"></a>2026-10-09 · `FJS-D698` — Which engine does the terminal runtime drive — OpenTUI's core alone, pinned to an exact version while it is 0.x, and never its React or Solid binding.

Asked in [`IDEAS/mesa-ir.md`](IDEAS/mesa-ir.md) § Open questions. **A** was picked over **B** (Ink. Mature, but it ships React under the runtime), **C** (write the cell buffer, layout and input ourselves. `FJS-D37` § 5 refuses this by name).

The paper's recommendation, taken as written: § 8 measured it doing every operation the runtime needs. A missing install fails through `missingPeer`.

### <a id="fjs-d692"></a>2026-10-09 · `FJS-D692` — A handler's event name passes through the IR as a DOM name and each non-DOM backend lowers it through its own table. The closed set of Gestures is read off the terminal's table and the phone's, never guessed before them.

Asked in [`IDEAS/mesa-ir.md`](IDEAS/mesa-ir.md) § Open questions (*a DOM event or a Gesture*). The paper's **A, then B** is taken, and the FJS Mobile report (artifact `5a2362a8`) adds the phone as the second input. Touch has gestures a terminal does not, like long-press and swipe. A closed set read off one backend's table would be missing them, so `FJS-D385`'s Gesture set is cut only once both tables exist. **C** (authors write `on:activate`) stays refused: it rewrites 216 handlers to fit a set nobody has measured.

### <a id="fjs-d555"></a>2026-09-29 · `FJS-D555` — `@money` has a built-in form control: sierra's table answers `money` and the kit binds it to `MoneyInput`. `@scale` keeps no control.

**Status:** amended-by [`FJS-D556`](#fjs-d556) — the bare-`@money` clause. There is no `USD` fallback, because a bare `@money` is refused at parse.

Asked in [`FJS-1582`](ISSUES_ARCHIVE.md#fjs-1582). A built-in control was picked over shipping `MoneyInput` for the app to register, which would have left a form putting cents in a dollar box until an app added two lines. It amends how `FJS-D17` was applied, not what it says: the table answered `control: null` for `@money` and left the control to the app, and every app that met that answer wrote the same box. An app still replaces it by registering `money`.

**The box is text in major units and hands back minor ones**, converted by the currency's ISO 4217 exponent. Blank is `null`. A value it cannot store exactly is refused through `reportInvalid` and never rounded: more decimals than the currency has, or `12,50`, which as grouping is 1250. `type="number"` would blank `1,200` and turn on scroll-wheel stepping.

**The currency rides on the table's answer** as `currency` / `currencyField`, spelled as in `displayFor`. A `@money(field: …)` column converts by its row's code: `FormField` hands a props builder the draft `record`, and when the code changes the amount on screen is kept and the minor value re-derived. A bare `@money` uses `USD`, which `<Cell>` and `formatMoney` also use. An app-level default is `FJS-1589`.

**`FilterBar`'s money range converts through the same two functions** and commits on `change`. It had filtered "from 10" as ten cents.

**`@scale` stays `control: null`.** Its number is money on some rows and a percentage on others (`example`'s `Discount.value`), and no app has written that control.

§ V answered before the first edit. The adjudication is *batteries vs. smallness*: this is a battery. Tier: Register. Question 9: a money box must write minor units. `packages/ui/test/browser/specs/money.spec.mjs` fails when it does not (8.29 → 829, 12.345 refused, the per-row re-derivation), and so do `filter-bar.spec.mjs` and sierra's `field-control-scaled.test.js`.

— `packages/sierra/src/resource/field-rules.js`, `packages/ui/components/forms/MoneyInput.mesa`, `FormField.mesa`, `display/FilterBar.mesa`.

### <a id="fjs-d404"></a>2026-09-25 · `FJS-D404` — A call follows the component's import watches: it re-runs when a `$:` on an import fires, wherever Mesa already re-runs it

Asked while weighing [`FJS-D371`](ISSUES.md#fjs-d371), by measuring what `{canEdit()}` does today. A function imported from another file reads what it reads out of the compiler's sight, so `{money(v)}` under `$: prefs.currency` subscribed to nothing. It moved only when another binding compiled into the same `render()` named `prefs`, which is an accident of grouping, and a call with arguments was classed static and written once. `example`'s `MoneyCell` declares `$: prefs.currency` as *load-bearing*, and measured, it moved nothing ([`FJS-1343`](ISSUES_ARCHIVE.md#fjs-1343)). **A** (a call to an import, or to a local function whose body reaches one, re-runs when the component's import watches fire) was picked over **B** (signals only: document *pass the store as an argument*, and keep the accident) and **C** (B, plus a warning on an imported call in a component that watches something).

The watch is already how a component says an import is live (`FJS-D381`), so A reads a declaration that exists rather than adding one, and whether a call is live stops depending on which bindings the compiler grouped, the same invisibility `FJS-D379` gave a throw. B leaves a screen correct or stale by what else is on it. C would fire on every formatter in a watching component. **A watch never makes anything reactive that was not**: it adds a trigger to a template binding, a prop and a derived `const`, and a static `const` stays a snapshot, since promoting one would make `const off = store.on(…)` lazy and re-subscribe it on every fire. A handler, a callback that runs later, `{#await}` and an async `const` are excluded, since a re-run there is a side effect or a request. **What A costs** is that every such call in a watching component re-runs when a watch fires, whether or not it reads the watched path. Measured over the repo, 71 render effects in 88 watching components gain a subscription, nearly all formatters; a 1000-row list of `{money(r.total)}` costs 1.6 ms per fire with a cached `Intl.NumberFormat` and 31 ms with one built per call. A narrower `$:` is the lever.

*Lives in:* `packages/mesa/docs/VISION.md` RULE 64 · `packages/mesa/src/compiler.js` (`WATCHED_CALLS` in `rewriteExpr`, `$$watches` in `emitScript`, `_isReactive`) · `packages/mesa/test/watch-follows-calls.test.js`

### <a id="fjs-d381"></a>2026-09-24 · `FJS-D381` — A component watches its imports itself; a cover it gets from another component's watch is incidental, kept as a feature, and measured rather than designed away

Asked while reading VISION RULES 44 and 47 against a scratch component that built `const doubled = store.count * 2` over an import and expected it to move. **RULE 44 stands**: an import is inert until a `$:` in THIS component watches it, and an imported primitive is a constant. Watching an import automatically wherever it is read was weighed and not taken — a library namespace, a config object and a class with private fields (RULE 49) would all be wrapped in a proxy they never asked for — and the per-component watch is what makes a component's reactivity readable from its own source.

**RULE 47 stays, and its text was wrong.** Measured (`packages/mesa/test/import-watch.test.js`): a component with no `$:` on an import reads the raw object and is never updated by any watch, so *"even components that declared nothing"* was false. The cross-component cover reaches only a component that watches ANOTHER path of the same import, and for that one it depends on mount order — mounted after the watcher it is covered, before it is not — and a watch is never unregistered, so the cover outlives the component that declared it. That is kept as a feature: a value this component does not watch shows its current value whenever something re-runs the binding, and the component did not ask for more. `$:` is how a component says it cares and `var` is how it says it wants the value as it was. **How often it matters is to be watched in real apps**; the count at the time of this ruling is in [`FJS-1340`](ISSUES_ARCHIVE.md#fjs-1340).

**Where a developer is told** (*doctrine vs. discovery*: the hearing amended the doctrine to match the code). The reads nothing watches are listed by the check that already owned the question — `_checkExternalReactivity`, whose strict level Sierra sets — extended to a top-level `const` and to a handler's deps as watches, and a dev build shows the list in the devtools panel beside the component. **No `fli check` rule**: a Sierra build already reports each read under strict, and a third surface grading the same question would be a second owner of it.

*Lives in:* `packages/mesa/docs/VISION.md` RULES 44 and 47 · `packages/mesa/src/compiler.js` `_checkExternalReactivity` · `packages/mesa/mesa-vite/devtools.html`

### <a id="fjs-d380"></a>2026-09-24 · `FJS-D380` — A kit control's one-way `value` is where it starts; a caller whose writes can be refused keeps a draft and puts it back

Asked in [`FJS-1336`](ISSUES_ARCHIVE.md#fjs-1336). A kit `<Select>` binds its `value` prop to its own copy, so a pick changes what is on screen whether or not the app keeps it.
